valid.name: fresh data-property definition - %HaveSameMap identical to plain assignment, measured safe
valid.code: const target = {}; Object.defineProperty(target, 'alpha', { value: 1, writable: true, enumerable: true, configurable: true });

valid.name: fresh non-enumerable data property - still %HasFastProperties true
valid.code: const target = {}; Object.defineProperty(target, 'hidden', { value: 1, enumerable: false, writable: false, configurable: false });

valid.name: two DIFFERENT fresh properties - neither redefines the other
valid.code: const target = {}; Object.defineProperty(target, 'alpha', { value: 1 }); Object.defineProperty(target, 'beta', { value: 2 });

valid.name: plain assignment is not this rule's concern
class accessor syntax - the compliant spelling for a getter
object-literal accessor syntax - also compliant, no defineProperty involved

invalid.name: redefinition of a property established earlier in the same scope
invalid.code: const target = {}; Object.defineProperty(target, 'alpha', { value: 1 }); Object.defineProperty(target, 'alpha', { value: 2 });

invalid.name: accessor descriptor with get - drops fast properties, 15.8x measured on reads
accessor descriptor with set
invalid.code: const target = {}; Object.defineProperty(target, 'alpha', { set(value) { void value; } });

invalid.name: accessor descriptor via Reflect.defineProperty - same hazard, different spelling
